questions.stem: Which is the correctly balanced equation for the combustion of methane?
questions.explanation: Check: Left side: 1C, 4H, 4O. Right side: 1C, 4H (2 x H₂O = 4H), 4O (2 from CO₂ + 2 from 2H₂O = 4O). Both sides balance with 1C, 4H, and 4O atoms. Option (a) is unbalanced (4H left, 2H right). You must never change the formulae of substances - only adjust the numbers in front.

questions.stem: Balance the equation: _Na + _H₂O → _NaOH + _H₂. What numbers go in the blanks?
questions.explanation: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Check: Left: 2Na, 4H, 2O. Right: 2Na, 2O (in NaOH), 2H (in NaOH) + 2H (in H₂) = 4H, 2O. All balanced. A common mistake is option (a), but checking: 1Na left, 1Na right (OK), but 2H + 1H = 3H on right vs 2H on left (unbalanced).

questions.stem: Why must chemical equations be balanced?

options.text: To make the equation look neat
Because atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction (conservation of mass)
To show that the products are heavier than the reactants
Because all reactions must have equal numbers of molecules on each side

questions.explanation: Chemical equations must be balanced because of the law of conservation of mass - atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. Every atom present in the reactants must appear in the products. The number of molecules does NOT need to be equal on each side; only the number of each type of atom must be the same.

questions.stem: What is the balanced equation for aluminium reacting with oxygen? _Al + _O₂ → _Al₂O₃
questions.explanation: 4Al + 3O₂ → 2Al₂O₃. Check: Left: 4Al, 6O. Right: 4Al (2 x 2), 6O (2 x 3). This equation is tricky because of the odd number of oxygens in Al₂O₃ (3), which means you need 2 of them to get an even number (6), then 3 O₂ molecules to provide 6 oxygens, and 4 Al atoms to match the 4 in 2Al₂O₃.

questions.stem: A student balances an equation by changing H₂O to H₂O₂. Why is this incorrect?

options.text: Because you must only change the large numbers in front of formulae, never the subscript numbers within formulae
Because H₂O₂ is a gas, not a liquid
Because the equation would have too many atoms

questions.explanation: When balancing equations, you can only change the coefficients (large numbers in front of formulae). Changing subscript numbers within a formula changes the substance itself. H₂O is water, but H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide - a completely different substance with different properties. The formulae of substances are fixed and must not be altered.
